chunks: Safwan narrated from Yahya al-Azraq from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him): Regarding a man who is killed while he has a debt and has not left any property, so his family takes the blood money (diyah) from his killer, is it upon them to pay his debt? He said: 'Yes.' I asked: 'And he left nothing?' He said: 'They only took his blood money, so it is upon them to pay his debt.'

key_terms.الدِّيَة: Blood money or compensation paid to the heirs of a victim of homicide or injury

ai.seo_question: What happens to the blood money if the deceased had unpaid debts and no other assets?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi records this ruling in the context of inheritance law, clarifying that blood money (diyah) is treated as the deceased's estate rather than a separate category of wealth. This ensures that creditors have priority over heirs, reflecting the Shia principle that debts must be settled from the deceased's assets before distribution, even if the only asset is the compensation received from the killer.
